summary: F1-F3 are fixed, but the new Forge gesture mapping changes the approved week 1 inset, and prepare depends on the optional handoff.
blocking_findings: F5 [Blocker] green: The intake adapter routes classmate cut-out gesture frames into ForgeArt.gestures and ForgeArt.idle. GestureInset.tsx:70-75 consumes those fields for the inset, replacing the approved Adventurer. The current week 1 scratch frame at frame 753 visibly shows a small classmate instead of the Adventurer. prepare.mjs:500-506 applies this handoff path to w01 when CLASS fallback names match available cast. Rationale: the plan requires week 1 to stay approved and the Adventurer inset to remain unchanged.

F6 [Blocker] green: prepare(rel) reads MANIFEST.tsv and the scene manifest unconditionally at prepare.mjs:500 and manifestToForgeInput:277-280. A missing handoff folder or MANIFEST.tsv therefore makes a normal render fail, including w01, despite the week having no handoff cast requirement. Rationale: the handoff is an optional art source and must not break existing weeks.
nonblocking_findings: F4 [Major] green: T2.6 still checks only the manifest path set and absence of Lily (tests/manifest-intake.test.mjs:137-143). A-F3 and A-F4 exercise preparation and copied-file hashes for w02 only (tests/forge-contracts.test.mjs:76-127), not the required per-week subsets for w03-w07. Rationale: the plan says T2.6 verifies actual copied files for weeks 2 to 7.

F7 [Major] green: The render-time copy path does not verify a copied file against its MANIFEST.tsv SHA. readManifestRows parses sha at prepare.mjs:251-255, but manifestToForgeInput ignores it at lines 283-305 and copyManifestSubset only copies bytes at lines 317-326. A-F4 hashes its w02 test copy (tests/forge-contracts.test.mjs:121-124), but prepare() does not enforce the check before a render. Rationale: changed or damaged handoff bytes can reach a render without an integrity failure.
evidence: F1 withdrawn: src/Actors.tsx:103-133 guards missing cast entries and draws a placeholder; tests/forge-contracts.test.mjs A-F1 passes.
F2 withdrawn: prepare.mjs:277-306 returns ForgeArt fields with project-relative paths; tests/forge-contracts.test.mjs A-F2 passes.
F3 withdrawn: tests/forge-contracts.test.mjs A-F3 calls prepare('l2/w02') and verifies Forge art; committed scripts/render.mjs still calls prepare(rel).
The T1.7 portrait assertions now use box.portrait and verify it against portrait lyrics, gesture, and the scene band (tests/bubbles.test.mjs:142-157).

The prepare snapshot test passes and matches fixture SHA-256 83f45092cd3047d25ee58249b0677e3e5cf43045d496c2d545f052173b4d8487, but it compares buildSpec output only (tests/prepare-snapshot.test.mjs:33-47); it does not pin prepare(rel)'s handoff-selected ForgeArt.

The week 1 evidence records four same-toolchain base/new equal pairs, but the evidence script prepares once with current code and copies current public/l2 assets into the base tree (green-p1-r2-w01-evidence.py:99-105). This masks changed preparation output.

green-p1-w01-compare.txt records 0 of 4 approved/current hash matches and PSNR 19.316 dB. The approved frame shows the Adventurer inset; the current frame shows a small classmate inset. The difference is visible and is not only subtle toolchain drift.
The missing-handoff failure follows from the unconditional reads at prepare.mjs:500 and manifestToForgeInput:277-280. No test covers absent handoff data.
A-F4 checks copied file hashes against MANIFEST.tsv for its w02 temp copy. Production prepare does not perform that comparison.

The production copy target is video/storytime-song/public/l2/<week>/forge/, inside the project. `git check-ignore -v` confirms video/storytime-song/.gitignore:10 (`public/l*/`) ignores the copied files, so they will not land in git.
HEAD is 4b25714b761231369540f0eadf2551d16379e7b4, equal to audited_head_sha. phase_base_sha resolves to 1ffd649b83df6f1f6625351d8da4afd5ee1ca513.
